perf.summary: Replace fractional Math.Pow root computations with integer nth-root via sqrt/cbrt to avoid expensive transcendental pow and floating-point rounding hazards.
perf.currentCost: Math.Pow(n, 0.25), Math.Pow(n, 0.5), Math.Pow(n, 1.0/3.0) and Math.Pow(w, 0.5) each invoke the general transcendental pow (exp/log pair, tens of cycles) inside the hot recursion, called O(n^(2/3)/log n) times overall.
perf.proposedChange: Compute b = isqrt(n) via long s=(long)Math.Sqrt((double)n) then while((s+1)*(s+1)<=n) s++; while(s*s>n) s--;. Compute c = icbrt(n) via (long)Math.Cbrt((double)n) with the same +/-1 correction loop. Compute a from c (fourth root = isqrt of icbrt-ish; or isqrt(b)). Reuse w's sqrt via isqrt(w) instead of Math.Pow(w,0.5).
perf.rationale: Math.Sqrt/Math.Cbrt are single hardware-friendly intrinsics far cheaper than generic pow; integer correction loops run 0-2 iterations. Removes log/exp dependency chains from the hottest recursion path.
perf.risk: Math.Pow with fractional exponents can round the boundary the wrong way (e.g. n^(1/3) for a perfect cube may yield k-epsilon truncating to k-1), so the current code may already be subtly off; the corrected integer-root loops both round UP and DOWN to land on the true floor, changing results only where Pow was already wrong. Validate against existing NUnit tests to confirm the intended floor semantics.

perf.summary: phiCache stores int values in a (PhiCacheSize)*(PhiCachePrimes+1) = 20000*101 layout; the stride is non-power-of-two forcing an imul on every index.
perf.currentCost: Every phiCache access computes m*(PhiCachePrimes+1)+a and (i/p)*(PhiCachePrimes+1)+j-1, i.e. a multiply by 101 (non-shiftable) plus add on each hot lookup and on every cell of the O(20000*100) init.
perf.proposedChange: Pad the row stride to 128 (next power of two >= 101) so index = (m<<7)+a becomes a shift+add; document the padded stride as a named const PhiCacheStride=128. Trade ~27% more cache footprint (2.08M -> 2.56M ints) for branch-free shift indexing, or alternatively keep 101 but precompute base = m*101 once per Phi call to hoist the multiply out of the cache-hit path.
perf.rationale: Multiply-by-constant 101 cannot be strength-reduced to a single shift; padding to 128 turns the address calc into a shift. On mobile (slower imul, weaker OOO) this matters in the inner init loop that touches 2M cells.
perf.risk: Larger cache uses more RAM/L2; on memory-constrained mobile the extra 1.9MB (int) may cause more cache misses than the multiply saves. Net win is data-dependent; flag for measurement. If padding, InitPhiCache and all index sites must use the same stride const consistently.
